name: coccinelle
desc: Program matching and transformation engine for C code
why: A semantic patch language that matches and rewrites C code by its structure, a real window into how Linux kernel changes are made.

brief.what_it_is: Coccinelle is a program matching and transformation engine for C code. It provides SmPL (Semantic Patch Language), which lets you describe a match on C code and the transformation to apply. Its input is C source plus a .cocci semantic patch, and its output is rewritten C source. The README calls it a tool for style-preserving source-to-source transformations, such as refactorings. The installed executables are spatch and spgen.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it was initially aimed at collateral evolutions in Linux: the changes client code needs when a library API changes, such as renaming a function, adding a context-dependent argument, or reorganizing a data structure. It also says the authors and others use it to find and fix bugs in systems code.
brief.how_it_works: You write a semantic patch in SmPL that describes code structure and the edit to make, then run spatch on the C files. The README says the transformations preserve the original source style. The README does not describe the matching internals further.

brief.install_notes: The README points to install.txt for building from source (not fetched). After installing, a spatch script goes in /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin. Precompiled binaries and distribution packages are listed at the project's download page. Optional runtime pieces: for OCaml scripting in SmPL, install ocaml-native-compilers or ocaml-nox; for Python scripting, install python3-dev (runtime only, not needed to build). Building the LaTeX docs needs texlive-fonts-extra and hevea. No accounts are needed.
brief.standout: Rather than matching text or regular expressions, it matches C code by its structure and rewrites it in place, keeping the original formatting. Its own homepage says semantic patches for Linux are kept in the kernel's scripts directory, so the tool is part of kernel development practice.
brief.status: Maintained, with weak evidence. The GitHub page is a mirror of the Inria repository and shows 7,832 commits, 821 stars, and a GPL-2.0 license. The fetched page did not show a last-commit date or a release date, so I could not confirm recent activity. The homepage has a Changelog, a Downloads page, and an Outreachy internship listing.
brief.caveats: The GitHub repository is a mirror; the main repository is at Inria. License: GPL-2.0 per the GitHub sidebar. Building from source needs install.txt, which I did not read. Scripting features depend on OCaml or Python. The docs need extra LaTeX packages. The Homebrew description gave no caveats. No platform limits appeared in what I read.
quotes: Coccinelle allows programmers to easily write some complex style-preserving source-to-source transformations on C source code, like for instance to perform some refactorings.
Coccinelle was initially targeted towards performing collateral evolutions in Linux.
Beyond collateral evolutions, Coccinelle is successfully used (by us and others) for finding and fixing bugs in systems code.
